items.title: Albert "June" Gardner Interview, 1996-04-17
items.q: he was good friends of my family... it was all like part of the family

ctx.x: One of those ones that you brought up in your hand?

Yeah, yeah. We had a lot of 78 Dr. Clayton records. Oh Dr. Clayton. Yeah. So all of the early big bands, I don't know what happened. Like I said, because we always had a piano at my house. It was always champion Jack Dupree used to stop by and play. Dupree? Oh yeah, he was good friends of my family. And he'd come in town, and when he lived here he would stay at my house. Really? Yeah, it was all like part of the family. I ran into him in Montrose, Switzerland a few years ago. He just died. Yeah, I know. But it…
Were you related to Dupree too?

items.title: Albert "June" Gardner Interview, 1996-04-17
items.q: Well he knew my mother and them before he knew me... We've just been friends. So long I can't just say, okay one day I was on the corner and he came up. He was always there. And he would play the piano and all the neighbors would come.

ctx.x: Well he knew my mother and them before he knew me. He knew my sisters, he knew my brothers. They knew him so long ago. I don't remember when they met. Like I said, it's like I know people in New Orleans. We've just been friends. So long I can't just say, okay one day I was on the corner and he came up. He was always there. And he would play the piano and all the neighbors would come. Miss Gordon always had something going on musically at the house. Nobody played music. But the piano was there.
Well I must have been experienced to listen to Champion Jack.

I sit right there and listen to all of it. Not only him, Toots Washington used to stop by. Toots? Yeah, Papa Yellow. Yeah, he touched. Yeah, that was my man, God bless him. And all of these guys, like I said, they had a smile and lures. I was very young and these guys would come and get me and it was an experience. And they all tell my mother, they'd take care of me. We used to go like the slide out, we'd make three dollars, five dollars for that night. Not be a child, you know, with these men. But they would all…

items.title: Albert "June" Gardner Interview, 1996-04-17
items.q: I came up with this, you know, like Jack the Cat.

ctx.x: How important was the radio? Did you listen to radio a lot as a kid?

Yeah, well, I came up with this, you know, like Jack the Cat. These guys used to play, this was before W-Y-L, D-W-M-R-Y, all the so-called black stations came on there. You had, it was limited, and it was rhythm and blues. Yeah. It wasn't rock and roll, you know, so it was limited. But you would catch some of the music that would play the rhythm and blues. But then I lived across the street from some juke joints, and all night long they played the blues. I could hear T-Bone Walker, Lil Green, Blue Lou Barker from…
What about phonograph records? Did you have a, was there a phonograph in your house?
